newsitem.title: DENMARK: Rare wedding letter by fairytale author found.
newsitem.headline: Rare wedding letter by fairytale author found.

text.p: A rare original letter by Danish 19th century fairytale writer Hans Christian Andersen congratulating a friend on his marriage has been discovered, a literary expert told Reuters on Tuesday.

The four-page letter, written in June 1859 by Andersen to a newly-married friend, the chief editor of a leading Danish newspaper, was recently found in the archives of the University of Odense in central Denmark, Andersen Centre leader Johan de Mylius said.

"Dear Most Happy Married Man! I would have written earlier but then I thought that a newly-wed couple would prefer to be left alone to coo together rather than be interrupted by a visit from an intruding carrier pigeon," Andersen wrote in the letter.

Andersen, Denmark's most celebrated author (1805-75), wrote thousands of letters during his life as well as being author of 156 fairytales still read all over the world, notably "The Ugly Duckling", "The Tin Soldier" and "The Snow Queen."
